sentences.text: Homework has never been terribly popular with students and even many parents, but in recent years it has been particularly scorned.

Text 2
P1 Pretty in pink: adult women do not remember being so obsessed with the colour, yet it is
pervasive in our young girls' lives. It is not that pink is intrinsically bad, but it is such a tiny slice of
the rainbow and, though it may celebrate girlhood in one way, it also repeatedly and firmly fuses girls'
identity to appearance. Then it presents that connection, even among two-year-olds, between girls as not
only innocent but as evidence of innocence. Looking around, I despaired at the singular lack of
imagination about girls' lives and interests.

红色本身并非坏事，但它只是彩虹中极小的一部分，尽管它可能在某种程度上赞颂女孩特质，但它也反复

象力的极度匮乏感到绝望。

practical matter, since the only way of getting clothes clean was to boil them. What's more, both boys

pink was actually considered the more masculine colour, a pastel version of red, which was associated
with strength. Blue, with its intimations of the Virgin Mary, constancy and faithfulness, symbolised
femininity. It was not until the mid-1980s, when amplifying age and sex differences became a dominant

女孩对粉红色的喜爱似乎不可避免，仿佛编码在她们的DNA中，但根据美国研究副教授Jo Paoletti的说

虑，所有婴儿都穿白色衣服,因为清洗衣物的唯一方法是煮沸它们。而且，男孩和女孩都穿被认为是中性的

乎天然地吸引女孩，成为定义她们作为女性的一部分，至少在最初几年的关键时期是如此。
P3 I had not realised how profoundly marketing trends dictated our perception of what is natural to
kids, including our core beliefs about their psychological development. Take the toddler. I assumed that
phase was something experts developed after years of research into children's behaviour: wrong. Turns

trick by clothing manufacturers in the 1930s.
我没有意识到市场营销趋势如此深刻地影响了我们对儿童天性的认知，包括我们关于他们心理发展的核心

据儿童消费主义历史学家Daniel Cook的说法，它是在20世纪30年代作为服装制造商的营销手段而流行起
来的。
P4 Trade publications counselled department stores that, in order to increase sales, they should
create a "third stepping stone" between infant wear and older kids' clothes. It was only after "toddler"
became a common shoppers' term that it evolved into a broadly accepted developmental stage. Splitting
kids, or adults, into ever-tinier categories has proved a sure-fire way to boost profits. And one of the
easiest ways to segment a market is to magnify gender differences – or invent them where they did not
previously exist.
行业刊物建议百货商店，为了增加销售额，它们应该在婴儿装和大龄儿童服装之间创造一个"第三个阶
梯"。只有在"学步儿童"成为购物者的常用术语之后，它才演变成一个被广泛接受的发展阶段。将儿童或
成人划分为越来越细小的类别已被证明是提高利润的可靠方法。而细分市场最简单的方法之一就是放大性
别差异——或者在以前不存在差异的地方创造出差异。

Directions:

"Universal history, the history of what man has accomplished in this world, is at bottom the History
of the Great Men who have worked here," wrote the Victorian sage Thomas Carlyle. Well, not any more
it is not.
维多利亚时代的智者托马斯·卡莱尔写道："世界历史，即人类在这个世界上所成就之事的历史，归根结底
是在此奋斗的伟人的历史。"然而，如今情况已不再如此。
Suddenly, Britain looks to have fallen out with its favorite historical form. This could be no more
than a passing literary craze, but it also points to a broader truth about how we now approach the past:
less concerned with learning from our forefathers and more interested in feeling their pain. Today, we
want empathy, not inspiration.
突然之间,英国似乎与其最钟爱的历史叙述形式决裂了。这也许只是一时的文学风潮,但它也指向了一个关
于我们如今如何看待过去的更广泛的真相:我们不再关注从先辈那里汲取教训,而是更感兴趣于感受他们的
痛苦。今天,我们要的是共情,而非激励。
From the earliest days of the Renaissance, the writing of history meant recounting the exemplary
lives of great men. In 1337, Petrarch began work on his rambling writing De Viris Illustribus – On
Famous Men, highlighting the virtus (or virtue) of classical heroes. Petrarch celebrated their greatness in
conquering fortune and rising to the top. This was the biographical tradition which Niccolò Machiavelli
turned on its head. In The Prince, he championed cunning, ruthlessness, and boldness, rather than virtue,
mercy and justice, as the skills of successful leaders.
从文艺复兴最早期开始,历史书写就意味着讲述伟人的典范生活。1337年,彼特拉克开始撰写其漫长的著作
《名人传》,突出古典英雄的美德。彼特拉克赞颂他们征服命运、登上巅峰的伟大之处。正是这一传记传统

被尼科洛·马基雅维利彻底颠覆。在《君主论》中,他推崇狡诈、无情和大胆,而非美德、仁慈和正义,将其视

Over time, the attributes of greatness shifted. The Romantics commemorated the leading painters and
authors of their day, stressing the uniqueness of the artist's personal experience rather than public glory.
By contrast, the Victorian author Samuel Smiles wrote Self-Help as a catalogue of the worthy lives of
engineers, industrialists and explorers. "The valuable examples which they furnish of the power of self-
help, of patient purpose, resolute working, and steadfast integrity, issuing in the formation of truly noble
and manly character, exhibit," wrote Smiles, "what it is in the power of each to accomplish for himself."
His biographies of James Watt, Richard Arkwright and Josiah Wedgwood were held up as beacons to
guide the working man through his difficult life.
随着时间推移,伟大的特质发生了转变。浪漫主义者颂扬当时杰出的画家和作家,强调艺术家个人体验的独
特性而非公众荣耀。相比之下,维多利亚时代作家塞缪尔·斯迈尔斯将《自助》写成工程师、实业家和探险
家高尚生活的汇编。斯迈尔斯写道:"他们所提供的关于自助之力、坚韧目标、坚定工作和坚贞正直的宝贵
范例,展现了真正高尚而刚毅品格的形成,说明每个人都有能力为自己成就些什么。"他为詹姆斯·瓦特、理查
德·阿克赖特和乔赛亚·韦奇伍德所作的传记被奉为指引工人阶级度过艰难人生的灯塔。
This was all a bit bourgeois for Thomas Carlyle, who focused his biographies on the truly heroic
lives of Martin Luther, Oliver Cromwell and Napoleon Bonaparte. These epochal figures represented
lives hard to imitate, but to be acknowledged as possessing higher authority than mere mortals.
这一切对托马斯·卡莱尔来说有些过于资产阶级化了,他的传记聚焦于马丁·路德、奥利弗·克伦威尔和拿破仑·
波拿巴真正英雄般的人生。这些划时代人物代表着难以效仿的生命,但应被承认拥有高于凡人的权威。
Not everyone was convinced by such bombast. "The history of all hitherto existing society is the
history of class struggles," wrote Marx and Engels in The Communist Manifesto. For them, history did
nothing, it possessed no immense wealth nor waged battles: "It is man, real, living man who does all
that." And history should be the story of the masses and their record of struggle. As such, it needed to
appreciate the economic realities, the social contexts and power relations in which each epoch stood. For:
"Men make their own history, but they do not make it just as they please; they do not make it under
circumstances chosen by themselves, but under circumstances directly found, given and transmitted from
the past."
并非所有人都被这种夸张言辞所说服。"迄今为止一切社会的历史都是阶级斗争的历史,"马克思和恩格斯在
《共产党宣言》中写道。对他们而言,历史什么也不做,它既不拥有巨大财富也不发动战争:"做这一切的是
人,是现实的、活生生的人。"而历史应该是大众及其斗争记录的故事。因此,它需要理解每个时代所处的经
济现实、社会语境和权力关系。因为:"人们自己创造自己的历史,但是他们并不是随心所欲地创造,并不是在
他们自己选定的条件下创造,而是在直接碰到的、既定的、从过去承继下来的条件下创造。
This was the tradition which revolutionised our appreciation of the past. In place of Thomas Carlyle,
Britain nurtured Christopher Hill, EP Thompson and Eric Hobsbawm. History from below stood
alongside biographies of great men. Whole new realms of understanding – from gender to race to
cultural studies – were opened up as scholars unpicked the multiplicity of lost societies. And it
transformed public history too: downstairs became just as fascinating as upstairs.
正是这一传统革新了我们对过去的理解。英国培养出了克里斯托弗·希尔、E.P.汤普森和埃里克·霍布斯鲍姆,
取代了托马斯·卡莱尔。自下而上的历史与伟人传记并驾齐驱。随着学者们剖析失落社会的多样性,从性别
到种族再到文化研究,全新的理解领域被开辟出来。这也改变了公共历史:楼下变得和楼上一样引人入胜。

P1 When people in developing countries worry about migration, they are usually concerned at the
prospect of their best and brightest departure to Silicon Valley or to hospitals and universities in the
developed world. These are the kind of workers that countries like Britain, Canada and Australia try to
attract by using immigration rules that privilege college graduates.
P2 Lots of studies have found that well-educated people from developing countries are particularly
likely to emigrate. A big survey of Indian households in 2004 found that nearly 40% of emigrants had
more than a high-school education, compared with around 3.3% of all Indians over the age 25. This
"brain drain" has long bothered policymakers in poor countries. They fear that it hurts their economies,
depriving them of much-needed skilled workers who could have taught at their universities, worked in
their hospitals and come up with clever new products for their factories to make.

compared with around 3.3% of all Indians over the age 25 这条比较状语在汉语里要靠「而 /

第 6 句开头用括注还原 They

全文围绕发展中国家的人才外流问题展开：第一段点出发展中国家最担心的是高学历精英流向英美
等发达国家（their best and brightest departure to Silicon Valley or to hospitals and
universities in the developed world），第二段用印度的调查数据和政策制定者的担忧加以佐证
（This "brain drain" has long bothered policymakers in poor countries）。基调是中性偏忧虑
的叙述，作者在转述这些国家的担心，而不是评判。
【术语】best and brightest = 最优秀人才
their best and brightest 是个熟词僻义型固定说法，不能按字面译成「最好和最聪明的
（人）」，而要统一译为「最优秀的人才 / 精英人才」；全文这条线索贯穿到第二段的 well-
educated people、skilled workers，译法上要让读者看出是同一类人。
These / they / them 的回指
第一段第二句 These are the kind of workers 中的 These 指代上一句的 their best and
brightest；第二段末句 depriving them of much-needed skilled workers 的 them 指代上一句
出现的 policymakers in poor countries / their economies 所对应的「这些贫穷国家」。这类
this/these/them 跨句指代必须回上一两句还原成具体名词再译，否则中文读起来悬空。
brain drain = 人才流失/人才外流
This "brain drain" 是全篇的术语锚点，原文加了引号，译文宜保留引号并统一译作「人才流失」
或「人才外流」，全篇前后用法一致，避免一处译「人才流失」、另一处译「智力外流」造成术语
漂移。
developing countries / poor countries 同指
developing countries 与 poor countries 在本文中所指相同，都是「发展中国家」；翻译时建议
统一处理为「发展中国家」，不要一处译「发展中国家」一处又译「贫穷国家」，以免读者误以为

难点：more than a high-school education 的边界
more than a high-school education 不是「比高中教育多」，而是「（学历）高于高中 / 高中
以上学历」，含本科、硕博等；对应中文常说「高中以上学历」。同时 nearly 40% 中 nearly 表
「将近 / 接近」，不能丢，也不能省成「40%」。
compared with around 3.3% of all Indians over the age 25.（比较状语（过去分词短语））★采分
→（这一比例）与 25 岁以上全体印度人中约 3.3% 形成对比
难点：compared with 的比较对象
compared with around 3.3% of all Indians over the age 25 中 compared with 引出比较对
象：把「移民中 40% 受过高中以上教育」与「25 岁以上印度人总体中只有 3.3% 受过高中以上
教育」相比，凸显移民群体的高学历比例远高于整体。主体考生易错点：①把 around 3.3% 漏
掉「约」字；②把 over the age 25 错译为「25 岁以下」；③不补出隐含的「同样的学历指
标」，导致比较的两组数据看起来不是同一回事。译时建议补「相比之下」或「而…仅」让对比
关系显化。
【调序】比较状语前置 + 数据对照显化
compared with around 3.3% of all Indians over the age 25 这条比较状语按汉语习惯放在主句
后用「相比之下 / 而…仅」承接更自然：主句先说「近 40% 的移民有高中以上学历」，再用「而
25 岁以上印度人总体中只有约 3.3%」做对比；也可以把比较的维度补出来——「（这一比例）远
高于…的 3.3%」让对照更直观。
【译文】2004 年针对印度家庭开展的一项大规模调查发现，移民中近 40% 的人拥有高中以上
学历，而 25 岁以上的印度人总体中受过同等教育的仅约 3.3%。

5. This "brain drain" has long bothered policymakers in poor countries.
【意群】This "brain drain"（主语（带引号术语））★采分→这种「人才流失」
难点：This 的回指 + 引号保留
This "brain drain" 中的 This 回指上一句所讲的现象——发展中国家受教育水平较高的人成批外
迁；翻译时可处理成「这种『人才流失』现象」，把引号一并保留，提示读者这是一个被普遍使
用的术语；不要省成「人才流失」三个字，会丢掉指代和引号两条信息。
has long bothered policymakers in poor countries.（主干 谓+宾 + 后置定语）★采分→长期以来
一直困扰着贫穷国家的政策制定者
难点：has long bothered 的时态语义
has long bothered 是现在完成时 + long，强调「长期以来一直 + 持续到现在仍在」，主体考
生要在汉语里加「长期以来 / 一直 / 多年来」这种时间副词把这层意思补出来；只译成「困扰」
会丢掉「长期」的信息。policymakers 译「政策制定者 / 决策者」均可。
【调序】状语 long 前移、宾语 in poor countries 前置
has long bothered policymakers in poor countries 英文里 long 紧贴助动词，in poor
countries 后置修饰 policymakers；汉译时按汉语习惯：①long 前移到句首作时间状语「长期以
来 / 多年来」；②in poor countries 前置作 policymakers 的定语「贫穷国家的（政策制定
者）」。整句调整后是「长期以来，这种『人才流失』一直困扰着贫穷国家的政策制定者」。
【译文】长期以来，这种「人才流失」一直困扰着贫穷国家的政策制定者。

6. They fear that it hurts their economies, depriving them of much-needed skilled workers who
could have taught at their universities, worked in their hospitals and come up with clever new
products for their factories to make.
【意群】They fear that it hurts their economies,（主句 + that 宾语从句）★采分→他们担心人才流失会
损害本国经济，
难点：They / it / their 的回指
They fear that it hurts their economies 中三个代词全部需要回指：They 指上一句的
policymakers in poor countries（贫穷国家的政策制定者），it 指上一句的 This "brain
drain"（这种人才流失），their 指 policymakers 所代表的「这些贫穷国家」。主体考生若不还
原，中文译出来会变成「他们担心它伤害他们的经济」，三个「他们/它」让人懵。译时建议把
They 还原成「这些政策制定者」或「他们（即上述政策制定者）」，it 还原成「这种现象 / 人
才流失」，their 还原成「本国 / 这些国家的」。
depriving them of much-needed skilled workers（现在分词短语作伴随状语）★采分→（人才流
失）使这些国家失去亟需的熟练劳动力
难点：deprive sb. of sth. 与 them 的回指
depriving them of much-needed skilled workers 是 deprive sb. of sth. 固定搭配 = 「剥夺
某人的某物 / 使某人失去某物」，主语承前是 it（即人才流失）；them 此处不是回指 They
(policymakers)，而是回指 their economies 或更上层的 poor countries，指「这些发展中国
家」。much-needed 是「亟需的 / 急需的」，skilled workers 是「技术工人 / 熟练劳动者 /
高技能人才」。这是全句最易出错的指代点。
who could have taught at their universities, worked in their hospitals and come up with clever
new products for their factories to make.（who 引导的定语从句，修饰 skilled workers）★采分→
这些技术工人本来可以在本国大学里执教、在本国医院里工作，还可以为本国工厂研发出巧
妙的新产品
难点：could have done 的虚拟语气
who could have taught at their universities, worked in their hospitals and come up with
clever new products for their factories to make 中 could have + 过去分词 是虚拟语气，表
示「本来可以…（但实际没有）」——这是本句的「灵魂语义」，正好对应「人才流失」造成的
损失：本来这些人才可以为本国大学、医院、工厂做贡献，结果都跑去发达国家了。主体考生必
须把「本来可以 / 原本可以」译出来，否则就把虚拟变成事实，意思就反了。come up with =
想出 / 研发出；for their factories to make 是不定式短语作 products 的后置定语 = 「供本国
工厂生产的（新产品）」。
【调序】分词短语转动词分句 + 定语从句独立译
depriving them of much-needed skilled workers who could have taught… and come up
with… 这段超长的「分词 + 长定语从句」按汉语习惯不能堆成一长串「…的…的」前置定语。主体
考生分两步：①把 depriving them of… 分词译成「使他们 / 这些国家失去…」的小分句，与主句
并列；②把 who 后的定语从句「拆出来另起一句」，让 skilled workers 这个名词独立承担「主
语」角色——「而这些（技术）工人本来可以…」。结果是「他们担心 + 这会损害本国经济 + 使
本国失去亟需的技术工人 + 而这些工人本来可以…」四个小分句铺开。

Section IV Part A
Directions:
Suppose you have found something wrong with the electronic dictionary that you bought from an online
store the other day. Write an email to the customer service center to
1) make a complaint, and
2) demand a prompt solution.
You should write about 100 words on ANSWER SHEET 2.
Do not sign your own name at the end of the letter. Use “Zhang Wei” instead.
Do not write your address. (10 points)

Dear Customer Service Center,
I am writing to complain about an electronic dictionary that I purchased from your online store last week.
Unfortunately, the product does not work properly. When I switch it on, the screen keeps flickering, and several
keys on the keyboard fail to respond, so I cannot look up any words at all.
